<?xml version="1.0"?>

  <RD format_version="3">
    <description>
                                                                                    The complex Ginzburg-Landau equation describes a vast variety of phenomena from nonlinear 
waves to second-order phase transitions, from superconductivity, superfluidity, and 
Bose-Einstein condensation to liquid crystals and strings in field theory. 
<a href="http://hopf.chem.brandeis.edu/yanglingfa/pattern/cgle/index.html">
[link]</a>
    </description>
    <rule name="Ginzburg-Landau" type="formula" wrap="1" neighborhood_type="vertex" neighborhood_range="1" neighborhood_weight="laplacian">
      <param name="timestep">
        0.15
      </param>
      <param name="alpha">
        0.1525
      </param>
      <param name="beta">
        0.92
      </param>
      <param name="delta">
        1.15
      </param>
      <param name="gamma">
        0.1775
      </param>
      <param name="D_a">
        0.075
      </param>
      <param name="D_b">
        1.3
      </param>
      <param name="rampPower">
        0.55
      </param>
      <param name="rampAlpha">
        0
      </param>
      <param name="rampBeta">
        0.01
      </param>
      <param name="rampDelta">
        0
      </param>
      <param name="rampGamma">
        0
      </param>
      <param name="rampD_a">
        0.2
      </param>
      <param name="rampD_b">
        0
      </param>
      <formula number_of_chemicals="4">
        //make the ramp
d = ( fabs(  ( ( get_global_id(0) * 1.0f) / ( get_global_size(0) * 1.0f ) )  - 0.5 ) * 2.0);
// apply power    
d = pow( d, rampPower );
//make derivs, applying the ramping
delta_a = (D_a + rampD_a * d) * laplacian_a + (alpha + rampAlpha * d)*a - (gamma + rampGamma * d)*b + (-(beta + rampBeta * d)*a + (delta + rampDelta * d)*b)*(a*a+b*b);
delta_b = (D_b + rampD_b * d) * laplacian_b + (alpha + rampAlpha * d)*b + (gamma + rampGamma * d)*a + (-(beta + rampBeta * d)*b - (delta + rampDelta * d)*a)*(a*a+b*b);
//make magnitude
c = sqrt(a*a + b*b);
      </formula>
      
    </rule>
